title: Data from Local System
summary: Data from Local System describes collecting files and information that already exist on a compromised host before exfiltration. The adversary searches the local file system, stored configuration, embedded databases, virtual machine disk images and process memory for documents, key material and records of interest, often driven by a command interpreter or by a network device command line that can read local storage. The activity is broad and mostly indistinguishable from ordinary administrator work, so detection depends on volume, scope and timing rather than on one suspicious action. Useful evidence includes enumeration commands, archive creation, staging directories, and unusually large reads from shares or database files. Baselining which accounts and processes normally touch sensitive paths is what makes an outlier visible at all.

beginner.definition: Local data means the files and information stored on the computer you are using. This technique is about an attacker searching that computer for useful files. The files are usually collected first and stolen later. It covers many kinds of local source, such as folders, databases and memory.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most valuable information sits on ordinary computers and servers. An attacker may collect quietly for weeks before stealing anything. The actions can look like normal administration work. Once files are collected, a single transfer can cause a large loss. Spotting collection early gives you time to block the theft.
howItWorks: The attacker gains access to a computer and opens a command or script shell.
They list drives, folders and network shares to learn what is available.
They search for interesting names, such as documents, keys or backups.
A local database, configuration file or virtual machine file may be read directly.
Useful files are copied into a temporary folder and often compressed together.
The collected package waits to be sent out of the network later on.
beginner.example: Picture a hotel night receptionist who wants to copy guest details. They do not empty the whole filing room. They walk the corridors and pick folders likely to hold passport copies and payment notes. Everything they gather is stacked in one cupboard, ready for a single trip to the car. The hotel looks normal until someone notices the cupboard. Local collection works the same way.
takeaways: Collection is quiet and can look like everyday file access.
Watch for large reads, new archives and unusual temporary folders.
Collected data can sit on a host for a long time before it leaves.

objectives: Explain what kinds of data an adversary collects from a local system.
Describe how command interpreters and device command lines support collection.
Explain why this collection stage is hard to separate from normal work.
Identify artefacts such as archives, staging folders and bulk file reads.
Describe how local collection supports a later exfiltration step.
